pictures.subject: backdrop
pictures.name: Tinker's Row
pictures.prompt: Repaint the image as a warm hand-painted storybook illustration in soft gouache, preserving every element of the layout exactly — every building footprint, wall, road, path, fence, doorway, and open ground area remains in precisely the same position, shape and size as shown. The mid-grey bands at the top and bottom of the canvas stay plain flat grey, unchanged. The black border region inside the grey but outside the map area stays dark. Only the visual treatment changes. The ground throughout the cobbled district of Tinker's Row becomes richly textured hand-painted setts of warm amber-grey stone, slightly uneven, with mortar cracks, oil-stained puddles catching lamplight, and the gentle worn hollows of a well-trodden pier district. The narrow lanes between buildings show cart-rut grooves, scattered brass filings, a dropped rivet or two, and faint chimney-soot deposits near pipe outlets. Cast shadows from buildings fall softly across the cobbles in warm amber-ochre afternoon light, consistent with a low southerly sun. All the rectangular building footprints — shown as flat boxes with blue-grey roofing and red front-wall bands — become proper workshop rooftops viewed from directly above: dark slate-grey or patinated copper-green pitched roofs with visible ridge lines, moss at the seams, weathered lead flashings, and squat brick chimney stacks trailing thin wisps of pale grey-cream smoke upward. Front walls (the south-facing red bands) become rendered stone or dark brick facades at the foot of each roof, each with a recessed framed door panel and one or two small brass-framed windows with warm amber glow leaking through frosted glass.

pictures.subject: backdrop
pictures.name: The Engine Cathedral
pictures.prompt: Repaint the reference image as a warm hand-painted storybook illustration in soft gouache, with visible brushwork, gentle overhead lighting, rich but muted colours, and tactile texture throughout, while keeping the layout pixel-faithful: every building footprint, wall line, fence, road, path, doorway, water feature and rock stays exactly where it is at exactly the same shape and size. The map area itself: the large rectangular enclosure that fills the centre of the image becomes the interior courtyard of the Engine Cathedral of Brasshaven, painted as worn dark-amber engineering brick laid in a herringbone pattern, cracked at the joints, oil-stained near the machinery clusters, with a faint sheen of condensation and scattered coal-dust. The golden dashed border around the enclosure becomes a low brass-capped stone kerb, catching warm lamp-glow from below. The outer surround of cobblestone-textured grey ground becomes soot-darkened city cobbles, wet and gleaming, with iron drain covers and tram-ruts pressed into the stone. Buildings: the six dark-blue-striped rectangular structures with red lower bands become the rooftops of iron-and-glass engine housings seen from directly above — their tops painted as riveted iron panels in deep slate-blue with amber brass bolt-heads along the seams, their red lower bands rendered as painted cast-iron fascias with green valve-handle details becoming actual small brass stopcocks and pressure gauges. The two lower-left and lower-right structures sit on patches of pale grey stone that become flagged maintenance yards, each centred on a dark lump that becomes a squat iron boiler dome, surrounded by scattered yellow lumps repainted as brass fittings, copper pipe coils and oily rags.

Paint the enclosing perimeter wall as mortared dark-grey stone with iron-railing sections along the top edge; the interior compound ground becomes worn, soot-stained dark-amber brick cobbles, cracked and oil-stained near the building entrances, with shallow puddles catching a dull amber glow from gas-lanterns mounted on short iron posts at the courtyard crossing — place those lanterns exactly where the small glowing object at the centre-cross and the golden object to the right already stand. A faint haze of coal smoke drifts from squat iron smokestacks rising from the rooftops of the six large rectangular buildings, each smokestack trailing a smudged charcoal plume toward the upper-right as though caught by a westerly breeze. pictures.subject: backdrop
pictures.name: The Skyport
pictures.prompt: Convert the entire image into a warm hand-painted storybook illustration in soft gouache with visible brushwork, gentle overhead lighting, and rich but muted colours, repainting every element of the top-down game map while preserving the layout with pixel-perfect fidelity: every building footprint, wall, fence, road, path, doorway, water feature and rock remains exactly where it is in the reference, at exactly the same shape and size. The wide cobblestone pier ground — currently rendered as flat grey tessellated stone — becomes aged, smoke-darkened basalt cobbles with iron-grey mortar, cracked at the joints, stained with rust streaks from chain and cable, scattered with wind-blown coal dust and the faint ghost of grease tracks where cargo carts have rolled; puddles sit in low joints, reflecting a warm amber-tinted overcast sky. The glowing dot-and-dash border running along the bottom edge and bottom-centre gap reads as a row of brass mooring-light lanterns set flush into the pier's lip, each casting a small honey-coloured pool onto nearby cobbles. The five large roofed rectangular buildings (three upper, two lower, plus the smaller one at lower-right) are repainted as high-altitude dockside warehouses of Brasshaven's Gilded Age: corrugated dark-slate roofs banded with aged copper ridge-caps, the roofing painted in deep teal and charcoal with warm brass trim lines exactly following the original stripe pattern; their south-facing front walls are broad brick facades in deep burgundy-red brick with arched loading-bay doors framed in wrought-iron — the door panels remain exactly where they are drawn, now rendered as heavy riveted iron doors with small brass portholes above. Each building casts a short, soft north-cast shadow onto the cobbles.

pictures.subject: backdrop
pictures.name: The Undercroft
pictures.prompt: Convert the entire image into a warm hand-painted storybook illustration rendered in soft gouache with visible brushwork, gentle lamplight, and rich but muted colours, preserving every element of the layout exactly — every catwalk platform, scaffolding bridge, building footprint, roofed box, framed door panel, barrel, bucket, and tree cluster stays in precisely its current position, shape and size, and the flat mid-grey bands at the top and bottom of the image remain plain mid-grey padding unchanged. Reinterpret the setting as The Undercroft of Brasshaven in the twenty-third year of the Gilded Age: a shanty town of wide timber catwalk platforms and narrow scaffolding bridges suspended in permanent darkness above an unseen void, viewed directly from above. The broad orange-brown platform surfaces become age-darkened hardwood planking with visible grain, iron nail heads, knothole stains, standing puddles of oily water catching amber light, and slow wisps of steam rising from grated vents set into the boards. Where the current image shows open dark void between platforms, paint deep blue-black darkness fading to near-black, with the faintest suggestion of dripping condensation and distant pipe-work far below. Edges of every catwalk and bridge show rough-cut timber ends, iron bracket mounts bolted to unseen stone piers, and fraying rope lashings. Buildings become low shanty structures of salvaged timber, corrugated iron sheeting, and scavenged brick, their roofs seen from above as patchwork surfaces of dark slate-grey tin, tarpaper, and mossy shingle with rusted flashing at ridges.
